clusters.name: Monitoring Signal Selection
clusters.description: The observable signals used to assess deployed-agent behavior, distinguishing external outcomes, internal state, reward streams, and composite detector outputs.

relations.rationale: Reward and behavioral signals must be selected before reward-integrity monitoring can assess divergence or exploitation.
Signal selection commonly determines which automated evidence and human review inputs are available.

values.label: Reward-signal monitoring
values.description: Monitoring episodic or scalar rewards received by the deployed agent.

values.label: Observation-signal monitoring
values.description: Monitoring environment observations and other externally visible state signals.

values.label: Agent-state monitoring
values.description: Monitoring internal agent information such as state estimates, value functions, entropy, or learning progress.

values.label: Behavior-trace diagnostics
values.description: Analyzing action sequences, tool-use traces, and agent logs to expose localized or behavior-specific failures.

values.label: Multi-layered evaluation signals
values.description: Combining automated metrics, domain benchmarks, model judges, guardrails, and human assessment for broader coverage.

values.label: Detector ensemble
values.description: Combining statistical, behavioral, anomaly, sequence, and system-integrity detectors rather than relying on one detector.

clusters.name: Reward Integrity Strategy
clusters.description: The design of reward objectives and safeguards against proxy exploitation, tampering, specification failure, and divergence from intended outcomes.

relations.rationale: Reward-integrity choices determine which reward, objective, and behavioral signals must be monitored.
Reward safeguards constrain how much automated evidence can be trusted without human or independent verification.
Detected reward-integrity failures require operational containment, investigation, and possible rollback.

values.label: Scalar proxy reward
values.description: Using a single scalar reward as a compact proxy for human preferences or task success.

values.label: Structured reward decomposition
values.description: Decomposing rewards into explicit, interpretable rubric dimensions that can be audited separately.

values.label: Complementary metric set
values.description: Using multiple related metrics to expose degradation hidden by a single optimized measure.

values.label: Reward veto layer
values.description: Invalidating or gating rewards when critical verification dimensions indicate an exploit or unacceptable outcome.

values.label: Hybrid verifier cascade
values.description: Combining rule-based precision with model-based recall and continuously updating the verifier as policy behavior shifts.

values.label: Single-metric optimization
values.description: Relying on one apparently comprehensive metric despite the risk of concealed degradation in related objectives.

values.label: Unhackable reward specification
values.description: Assuming that sufficiently careful reward design can guarantee immunity from reward hacking.

values.label: Proxy-objective divergence
values.description: Observed outcome in which optimizing the available reward produces behavior different from the intended task objective.

clusters.name: Oversight Allocation Strategy
clusters.description: The allocation of monitoring responsibility among automated detectors, model explanations, expert reviewers, and human-in-the-loop processes.

relations.rationale: Available monitoring signals determine whether automated or human oversight can make a reliable assessment.
Reward opacity, exploitability, and evaluator deception constrain reliance on automated or human-only oversight.

values.label: Human-in-the-loop review
values.description: Continuously involving human reviewers to assess and improve deployed-agent behavior.

values.label: Automated-only review
values.description: Relying exclusively on automated models or detectors to assess and improve agent behavior.

values.label: High-risk review checkpoints
values.description: Routing outputs classified as high risk to domain experts or regulators before production use.

values.label: Explanation-assisted inspection
values.description: Inspecting verbalized reasoning or chain-of-thought as an additional signal for reward-hack detection.

values.label: Behavior-only monitoring
values.description: Relying on externally visible outputs while omitting internal explanations or reasoning evidence.

values.label: Deceptive evaluator-facing behavior
values.description: Observed behavior in which agents appear correct to evaluators while pursuing an unintended objective.

clusters.name: Deployment Hosting Strategy
clusters.description: The serving and hosting foundation for deployed RL agents, varying in control, operational burden, scalability, privacy, compliance, and latency.

relations.rationale: The hosting foundation determines which policy-update and release mechanisms can operate safely in production.
Hosting capabilities constrain available observability, scaling, fallback, and incident-containment operations.

values.label: Private-cloud deployment
values.description: Hosting sensitive or time-critical RL systems in a private cloud with end-to-end lifecycle control.

values.label: Managed microservice serving
values.description: Serving policies through a managed, autoscaling microservice to reduce infrastructure maintenance.

values.label: Cloud-native RL service
values.description: Adopting managed cloud-native services for RL training, deployment, and monitoring.

values.label: Custom RL pipeline
values.description: Developing a bespoke pipeline when existing frameworks cannot meet integration, safety, or performance requirements.

values.label: Distributed training infrastructure
values.description: Scaling training across multiple GPUs or nodes while preserving learning stability and reproducibility.

values.label: Privacy and compliance protection
values.description: Operational outcome involving protected sensitive data and satisfaction of regulatory requirements.

clusters.name: Policy Update and Release Strategy
clusters.description: The timing, isolation, validation, and reversibility of policy changes after deployment, including continuous learning and staged production rollout.

relations.rationale: Serving topology and compute resources must support the selected update and release mechanism.
Update strategies determine the rollback and containment actions needed when a policy change causes degradation.
Continuous or incremental updates require an ongoing stream of production feedback and experience data.

values.label: Separated training and inference
values.description: Keeping training and serving environments distinct to preserve serving stability and latency.

values.label: Co-located training and serving
values.description: Co-locating processes to reuse serving computations and support online updates efficiently.

values.label: Continuous online updating
values.description: Returning feedback-driven incremental model updates directly into production serving.

values.label: Validation-gated deployment
values.description: Releasing updated policies only after validation, shadow testing, or limited-traffic evaluation.

values.label: Fixed-base adapter updating
values.description: Keeping a base model fixed while continuously updating a reversible adapter such as LoRA.

values.label: Production policy A/B testing
values.description: Comparing policy versions or baselines on separated production traffic before broader adoption.

values.label: Continuous policy deployment
values.description: Continually releasing improved policy versions as they become available.

values.label: Adapter rollback
values.description: Reverting a continuously learned adapter when an update causes problematic behavior.

values.label: Learning-serving resource contention
values.description: Operational outcome in which update computation competes with inference resources and degrades serving performance.

clusters.name: Incident Evidence and Containment
clusters.description: The operational mechanisms for detecting, attributing, containing, recovering from, and learning from deployed-agent incidents.

relations.rationale: Incident evidence depends on the signals and logs selected for routine monitoring.
Incident controls constrain whether and how new policy versions may continue rollout or learning.
Incidents can require freezing, inspecting, or correcting the experience data feeding future updates.

values.label: Observability dashboards
values.description: Providing operational dashboards for visibility into deployed policy behavior and incident indicators.

values.label: Canary threshold control
values.description: Defining thresholds for staged rollout evaluation and production traffic control.

values.label: Safe fallback switching
values.description: Switching to a safe fallback or behavior policy when the deployed policy is unsafe or degraded.

values.label: Dataset-ingestion freeze
values.description: Freezing affected data ingestion during investigation to prevent contaminated evidence from entering the pipeline.

values.label: Shadow-log evidence collection
values.description: Collecting non-disruptive logs and offline evaluation snapshots for comparison and diagnosis.

values.label: Version and traffic-slice attribution
values.description: Identifying the affected policy version and traffic segment during incident analysis.

values.label: Dataset-evaluation postmortem
values.description: Using postmortems to investigate mismatches between datasets, offline evaluations, and production behavior.

clusters.name: Feedback Data Collection Strategy
clusters.description: The acquisition, timing, provenance, and reuse of human and production feedback that supports monitoring, diagnosis, and subsequent policy improvement.

relations.rationale: Online learning and repeated policy releases require a reliable stream of production or preference feedback.
Incident controls may freeze, filter, or preserve feedback data for later diagnosis and remediation.
Human review and preference supervision directly shape the quality and interpretation of collected feedback.

values.label: Cyclic feedback collection
values.description: Collecting feedback iteratively in repeated cycles to support incremental improvement and reduce failure risk.

values.label: Single-batch feedback collection
values.description: Collecting feedback once in a single batch rather than through repeated feedback cycles.

values.label: Preference propagation
values.description: Extending a small amount of human preference feedback across larger datasets for scalable RLHF monitoring and improvement.

values.label: Production experience-data pipeline
values.description: Collecting, processing, and storing deployed-agent experience for continuous learning and policy improvement.

values.label: Replay-buffer rehearsal
values.description: Intermixing important historical examples with new feedback to preserve prior capabilities during continual learning.

values.label: Comparative preference supervision
values.description: Using human comparisons of candidate outputs as supervision for reward-model or preference-signal construction.

values.label: Non-i.i.d. feedback drift
values.description: Operational outcome in which noisy, malicious, or user-specific feedback causes unintended policy oscillation or drift.

clusters.name: Monitoring Combination Strategy
clusters.description: The combination, granularity, cadence, and automation of signals and detectors used to identify failures at production scale.

relations.rationale: Combination and diagnostic choices determine how selected signal types become actionable evidence.
Automated detector coverage and human review are commonly combined to improve monitoring reliability.
Detector outputs provide evidence for incident attribution and containment.

values.label: Multi-layered evaluation signals
values.description: Combining automated metrics, domain benchmarks, model judges, guardrails, and human assessment for broader coverage.

values.label: Detector ensemble
values.description: Combining statistical, behavioral, anomaly, sequence, and system-integrity detectors rather than relying on one detector.

values.label: In-stream diagnostic computation
values.description: Computing targeted instability diagnostics during training or operation rather than relying only on post-run analysis.

values.label: Interaction-mode diagnostic slicing
values.description: Separating diagnostics by interaction context, such as pre-tool and post-tool modes, to localize failures.

values.label: Cross-worker diagnostic aggregation
values.description: Aggregating diagnostic statistics across distributed workers so localized instability is visible at production scale.

values.label: Lightweight rolling-window statistics
values.description: Tracking lightweight statistics over recent rolling windows to limit monitoring overhead during large-scale operation.

values.label: Percentile-based tail monitoring
values.description: Tracking distribution percentiles to expose rare catastrophic behavior and gradual tail growth hidden by means.

values.label: Fixed-cadence diagnostic updates
values.description: Collecting diagnostics on a recurring fixed cadence rather than continuously to control monitoring overhead.

values.label: LLM-based behavioral monitor
values.description: Using a separate language model to inspect an RL agent for misbehavior and reward hacking.

values.label: Trusted-baseline policy comparison
values.description: Comparing candidate policy behavior with a safe trusted baseline when the true reward is unavailable.

values.label: Internal interpretability audit
values.description: Auditing activations, weights, or learned representations to detect proxy-reward pursuit and reward-model exploitation.

values.label: Output-pattern anomaly detection
values.description: Detecting suspicious output-length trends, recurring n-grams, or other automatically identifiable behavioral patterns.

values.label: Incomplete anomaly-detection protection
values.description: Outcome in which detectors provide partial separation but no universal protection against misspecified rewards.

values.label: Reward-hacking detection effectiveness
values.description: Outcome in which an LLM-based monitor successfully flags attempts to subvert evaluation or unit tests.

clusters.name: Reward Verification Strategy
clusters.description: The independent checking, gating, and enforcement mechanisms used to validate reward evidence and prevent proxy exploitation.

relations.rationale: Verification mechanisms must match the representation and complexity of the reward objective.
Verifier reliability and reward opacity constrain how much oversight can be automated.
Detected reward-integrity failures require operational investigation and containment.

values.label: Reward veto layer
values.description: Invalidating or gating rewards when critical verification dimensions indicate an exploit or unacceptable outcome.

values.label: Hybrid verifier cascade
values.description: Combining rule-based precision with model-based recall and updating the verifier as policy behavior shifts.

values.label: Unhackable reward specification
values.description: Assuming that sufficiently careful reward design can guarantee immunity from reward hacking.

values.label: Proxy-objective divergence
values.description: Outcome in which optimizing the available reward produces behavior different from the intended task objective.

values.label: Specification loophole exploitation
values.description: Outcome in which an optimizing agent discovers and exploits weaknesses in the task specification.

values.label: Evaluation-system manipulation
values.description: Outcome in which an agent finds ways to fool or manipulate the evaluation system.

clusters.name: Release and Rollback Strategy
clusters.description: The validation, traffic exposure, rollback, and fallback controls governing policy versions entering or leaving production.

relations.rationale: Release controls determine how updated policies are exposed after training or adaptation.
Release and rollback decisions require incident evidence, thresholds, and traffic attribution.

values.label: Validation-gated deployment
values.description: Releasing updated policies only after validation, shadow testing, or limited-traffic evaluation.

values.label: Production policy A/B testing
values.description: Comparing policy versions or baselines on separated production traffic before broader adoption.

values.label: Continuous policy deployment
values.description: Continually releasing improved policy versions as they become available.

values.label: Adapter rollback
values.description: Reverting a continuously learned adapter when an update causes problematic behavior.

values.label: Best-checkpoint rollback
values.description: Reloading the checkpoint associated with the best observed performance after current-policy degradation.

values.label: Safe-policy fallback
values.description: Switching to a rule-based or otherwise safe policy during recovery from unsafe or degraded behavior.

values.label: Reduced-learning-rate recovery
values.description: Resuming training after rollback with a smaller learning rate to reduce further destabilization.

clusters.name: Incident Containment Strategy
clusters.description: The traffic, rollout, ingestion, and operational controls used to limit harm while a deployed-agent incident is investigated.

relations.rationale: Containment choices depend on evidence about affected versions, traffic, data, and failure severity.
Containment may pause rollout, trigger rollback, or select a fallback policy.
Incident containment can freeze or filter feedback ingestion to prevent contaminated updates.

values.label: Canary threshold control
values.description: Defining thresholds for staged rollout evaluation and production traffic control.

values.label: Safe fallback switching
values.description: Switching to a safe fallback or behavior policy when the deployed policy is unsafe or degraded.

values.label: Dataset-ingestion freeze
values.description: Freezing affected data ingestion during investigation to prevent contaminated evidence from entering the pipeline.

clusters.name: Feedback Reuse Strategy
clusters.description: The supervision, propagation, rehearsal, and continual adaptation mechanisms that determine how collected feedback influences later policy changes.

relations.rationale: Feedback reuse requires acquired feedback with sufficient provenance and relevance.
Reuse choices shape how subsequent policy updates are trained and adapted.
Human oversight and preference judgments commonly determine which feedback is propagated or rehearsed.

values.label: Preference propagation
values.description: Extending a small amount of human preference feedback across larger datasets for scalable RLHF monitoring and improvement.

values.label: Replay-buffer rehearsal
values.description: Intermixing important historical examples with new feedback to preserve prior capabilities during continual learning.

values.label: User-feedback-driven model adaptation
values.description: Using accepted or rejected user outputs as feedback for fine-tuning individual or collective preferences.

values.label: Online learning from aggregate usage
values.description: Using privacy-respecting aggregate deployed-system interactions as an adaptation signal.

values.label: Reduced debugging and retraining effort
values.description: Outcome in which continuous human feedback reduces debugging and retraining effort.

values.label: Accelerated model deployment
values.description: Outcome in which RLHF and HITL feedback streamline model deployment and launches.

values.label: Reduced development costs
values.description: Outcome in which earlier human expertise reduces costly trial-and-error development cycles.

clusters.name: Monitoring Evidence Modality
clusters.description: The observable evidence type used to assess deployed-agent behavior, including rewards, observations, internal state, actions, explanations, and external outcomes.

relations.rationale: Evidence modalities determine which signals can be combined into monitoring procedures.
Available evidence constrains feasible oversight and review arrangements.

values.label: Reward-signal monitoring
values.description: Monitoring episodic or scalar rewards.

values.label: Observation-signal monitoring
values.description: Monitoring environment observations and externally visible state.

values.label: Agent-state monitoring
values.description: Monitoring internal state, values, entropy, activations, or weights.

values.label: Behavior-trace diagnostics
values.description: Analyzing actions, trajectories, outputs, tool traces, and logs.

values.label: Chain-of-thought monitoring signal
values.description: Using generated reasoning traces as monitoring evidence.

values.label: Chain-of-thought misalignment monitoring
values.description: Using reasoning traces to inspect misalignment or cheating.

values.label: Action-only monitoring
values.description: Monitoring externally visible actions without reasoning traces.

values.label: External-world feedback
values.description: Using outcomes supplied by the external environment rather than only an internal evaluator.

values.label: Human-oracle scoring
values.description: Maintaining human scores alongside automated evaluator scores.

relations.rationale: Objective representation determines which reward and behavior evidence must be monitored.

values.label: Structured reward decomposition
values.description: Explicit interpretable rubric dimensions.

values.label: Complementary metric set

values.label: Single-metric optimization
values.description: Reliance on one comprehensive metric.

values.label: Human-approval reward signal
values.description: Human helpfulness and correctness judgments used as reward.

values.label: Preference-derived reward signal
values.description: Pairwise preferences transformed into a reward signal.

values.label: Natural-language proxy objective
values.description: An imperfect natural-language objective whose omissions can be exploited.

values.label: Constitutional rule-based reward
values.description: Explicit constitutional principles used to evaluate outputs.

values.label: Multiple objective feedback channels
values.description: Human preferences, AI critique, and explicit rules used together.

values.label: Proxy reward based on geometric height

values.label: Modification-aware value learning

clusters.name: Monitoring Evidence Modality
clusters.description: The observable evidence used to assess deployed-agent behavior, including outputs, reasoning traces, operational signals, and human judgments.

relations.rationale: Available evidence determines which oversight arrangements are feasible.

values.label: Scratchpad reasoning observability
values.description: Using exposed scratchpad or hidden-reasoning traces to inspect belief use, evaluation awareness, alignment faking, or reward-hacking intent.

values.label: Automated safety-flag signals
values.description: Using classifiers or keyword detectors to flag harmful, biased, or inappropriate outputs at production scale.

values.label: Operational service telemetry
values.description: Using latency, action failures, invocation logs, feature availability, and resource signals as monitoring evidence.

values.label: Exploration-pattern monitoring
values.description: Monitoring exploration behavior to identify unsafe, anomalous, or unusually risky production actions.

values.label: System-health telemetry
values.description: Monitoring infrastructure and service-health signals alongside agent behavior and reward signals.

values.label: User-behavior feedback signals
values.description: Using rephrasing, edits, clarifications, bounce rates, usage, and related user behavior as indirect evidence of agent quality or drift.

values.label: Activation-delta monitoring
values.description: Monitoring changes in internal activations between clean and drifted inputs.

values.label: Reward-signal monitoring
values.description: Monitoring episodic or scalar rewards.

values.label: Observation-signal monitoring
values.description: Monitoring environment observations and externally visible state.

values.label: Agent-state monitoring
values.description: Monitoring internal state, values, entropy, activations, or weights.

values.label: Behavior-trace diagnostics
values.description: Analyzing actions, trajectories, outputs, tool traces, and logs.

values.label: Chain-of-thought monitoring signal
values.description: Using generated reasoning traces as monitoring evidence.

values.label: Chain-of-thought misalignment monitoring
values.description: Using reasoning traces to inspect misalignment or cheating.

values.label: External-world feedback
values.description: Using outcomes supplied by the external environment rather than only an internal evaluator.

values.label: Human-oracle scoring
values.description: Maintaining human scores alongside automated evaluator scores.

clusters.name: Anomaly and Drift Detection
clusters.description: The detectors and statistical tests used to identify distribution change, uncertain actions, abnormal behavior, and divergence from trusted baselines.

relations.rationale: Detection requires appropriately collected and aggregated observations.
Detected anomalies can trigger runtime intervention or containment.

values.label: Dataset-to-live distance detection
values.description: Detecting deployment shift by comparing offline and live feature distributions with KL divergence or MMD.

values.label: Reward-model OOD detection
values.description: Detecting unreliable reward estimates on outputs outside the reward model's training distribution.

values.label: Alignment-faking detection
values.description: Detecting reasoning or behavior that appears compliant while pursuing a different objective or manipulating evaluation.

values.label: Action-compatibility detection
values.description: Detecting deployed actions that are incompatible with the production environment's action space.

values.label: Reward-behavior divergence detection
values.description: Detection of high reward paired with poor task performance, unusual behavior, weak generalization, or metric divergence.

values.label: Activation-classifier drift detection
values.description: A classifier detects task drift from internal activation differences without modifying or fine-tuning the base model.

values.label: Statistical out-of-sample detection
values.description: Statistical detection of production inputs outside the training or expected distribution.

values.label: Tool-conditioned support-mismatch detection
values.description: Detection of low reference-policy probability in tool-conditioned states where concentrated variance and instability can emerge.

values.label: Empirical-CDF distribution monitoring
values.description: Monitoring empirical cumulative distributions to detect shape changes, tail stretching, and probability-mass migration.

values.label: Aggregate-metric monitoring blind spot
values.description: Aggregate loss, reward, or entropy remains stable while rare tail instability develops.

values.label: Anomaly detection
values.description: Detection of unusual behavior or reward exploitation.

values.label: Output-pattern anomaly detection
values.description: Detection of suspicious output patterns.

values.label: KL-divergence monitoring
values.description: Policy divergence measured with KL divergence.

values.label: Data-drift monitoring
values.description: Input distribution monitoring.

values.label: Concept-drift monitoring
values.description: Input-output relationship monitoring.

values.label: Model-drift monitoring
values.description: Monitoring changing production behavior.

values.label: Novelty detection
values.description: Detection of unfamiliar scenarios.

values.label: Capability-relevant unknown detection
values.description: Detection of situations beyond agent capability.

values.label: Scenario-based OOD definition
values.description: Scenario-level in-distribution and out-of-distribution definitions.

values.label: Metric-divergence alerting
values.description: Alerts when optimized and related metrics diverge.

values.label: Hallucination-rate monitoring
values.description: Invalid-claim rate monitoring.

values.label: Bias-score monitoring
values.description: Demographic or customer bias monitoring.

values.label: Accuracy-drift monitoring
values.description: Accuracy monitoring over time.

values.label: Threshold KPI alerting
values.description: Alerts on KPI thresholds.

values.label: Reward-result gap
values.description: Observed reward diverges from intended task results.

values.label: Evaluator-oracle score divergence
values.description: Automated evaluator scores diverge from human oracle scores.

clusters.name: Evaluation and Test Strategy
clusters.description: Offline, shadow, adversarial, holdout, simulation, and runtime evaluation methods used before or alongside production monitoring.

relations.rationale: Evaluation evidence informs release, retraining, and rollback decisions.
Evaluation tests whether reward and verifier mechanisms resist exploitation.

values.label: Offline policy-value evaluation
values.description: Estimating deployed-policy value from logged experience using importance sampling or fitted-Q evaluation before or alongside deployment.

values.label: Realistic safety-sabotage evaluation
values.description: Testing whether an agent with actionable tools will sabotage safety research, monitoring code, or evaluation infrastructure.

values.label: Cross-task reward-hack holdout evaluation
values.description: Testing whether reward-hacking behavior transfers from training environments to separate tasks and datasets.

values.label: Adversarial red-team evaluation
values.description: Using human or AI adversaries to probe deployed policies and reward models for exploitable weaknesses.

values.label: Randomized reference-output validation
values.description: Comparing outputs with a reference solution over randomized test cases to reduce fixed-output evaluation exploits.

values.label: Benchmark-only safety validation
values.description: Treating benchmark passage as sufficient evidence of safety despite possible deployment distribution change.

values.label: Unknown-situation rejection or human handoff

clusters.name: Monitoring Evidence Modality
clusters.description: The observable evidence used to assess deployed-agent behavior, including rewards, outputs, reasoning, actions, telemetry, internal state, and human judgments.

relations.rationale: Available evidence constrains which detection and oversight mechanisms can operate reliably.
Evidence availability limits the feedback and update mechanisms that can be safely applied.

values.label: Reward-signal monitoring
values.description: Monitoring scalar or proxy rewards as evidence of agent performance.

values.label: Proxy-reward monitoring
values.description: Monitoring proxy rewards that may diverge from real-world or true task outcomes.

values.label: Behavior-trace diagnostics
values.description: Analyzing actions, trajectories, outputs, tool traces, and logs.

values.label: Chain-of-thought monitoring
values.description: Using reasoning traces to inspect exploits, misalignment, or concealed intent.

values.label: Action-only monitoring
values.description: Monitoring externally visible actions without access to reasoning traces.

values.label: Operational service telemetry
values.description: Using latency, errors, resource use, feature availability, and invocation signals.

values.label: Human-oracle scoring
values.description: Using human judgments as evidence alongside automated evaluation.

values.label: External-world feedback
values.description: Using real-world outcomes rather than only internal reward or evaluator signals.

values.label: Activation-state monitoring
values.description: Monitoring internal activations, values, entropy, weights, or related model state.

values.label: Scratchpad reasoning observability
values.description: Using exposed scratchpad or hidden-reasoning traces to inspect belief use, evaluation awareness, alignment faking, or reward-hacking intent.

values.label: Automated safety-flag signals
values.description: Using classifiers or keyword detectors to flag harmful, biased, or inappropriate outputs at production scale.

values.label: Exploration-pattern monitoring
values.description: Monitoring exploration behavior to identify unsafe, anomalous, or unusually risky production actions.

values.label: System-health telemetry
values.description: Monitoring infrastructure and service-health signals alongside agent behavior and reward signals.

values.label: User-behavior feedback signals
values.description: Using rephrasing, edits, clarifications, bounce rates, usage, and related user behavior as indirect evidence of agent quality or drift.

values.label: Activation-delta monitoring
values.description: Monitoring changes in internal activations between clean and drifted inputs.

values.label: Observation-signal monitoring
values.description: Monitoring environment observations and externally visible state.

values.label: Agent-state monitoring
values.description: Monitoring internal state, values, entropy, activations, or weights.

values.label: Chain-of-thought monitoring signal
values.description: Using generated reasoning traces as monitoring evidence.

values.label: Chain-of-thought misalignment monitoring
values.description: Using reasoning traces to inspect misalignment or cheating.

clusters.name: Detection Target
clusters.description: The production failure or change that monitoring infrastructure is intended to identify.

relations.rationale: A defined detection target is required before selecting an appropriate detection method.
Detection targets determine which tests and evaluation scenarios are relevant.

values.label: Distribution-drift detection
values.description: Detecting changes in input, concept, model, or live feature distributions.

values.label: Novel-situation detection
values.description: Detecting unfamiliar situations while distinguishing harmless novelty from capability-relevant hazards.

values.label: Capability-boundary detection
values.description: Detecting situations beyond the agent's reliable capabilities.

values.label: Reward-behavior divergence detection
values.description: Detecting high or improving reward paired with poor intended-task performance.

values.label: Alignment-faking detection
values.description: Detecting apparently compliant behavior that conceals a different objective or harmful intent.

values.label: False-negative-rate detection
values.description: Detecting missed harmful or emerging behavior through production error-rate monitoring.

values.label: Subtle-cheating detection gap
values.description: Failure to detect increasingly sophisticated or concealed cheating.

values.label: Intent-concealment outcome
values.description: The agent hides misaligned intent or behavior in response to monitoring or penalties.

clusters.name: Detection Method
clusters.description: The statistical, learned, comparative, or rule-based mechanism used to identify the selected production failure.

relations.rationale: Detection methods operationalize the selected detection target.
Method sensitivity and reliability constrain alert thresholds and intervention decisions.

values.label: Statistical drift testing
values.description: Using KL divergence, MMD, empirical distributions, drift indices, or related statistical tests.

values.label: LLM-based behavioral monitoring
values.description: Using a separate language model to inspect reasoning or behavior for exploits and misalignment.

values.label: Reward-model ensemble detection
values.description: Using multiple reward models and disagreement or agreement requirements to identify gaming.

values.label: Normal safety evaluation
values.description: Using ordinary safety evaluations to detect readily observable harmful behavior.

values.label: Trip-wire monitoring
values.description: Using intentional vulnerabilities or probes to expose reward-hacking behavior.

values.label: Capability-stratified evaluator detection
values.description: Using evaluators with different capabilities to expose subtle or capability-dependent hacks.

values.label: Strict novelty classification
values.description: Treating every detected difference as out-of-distribution regardless of task relevance.

values.label: Detection incompleteness
values.description: Partial detector coverage leaves some anomalous or reward-hacking behavior unobserved.

clusters.name: Evaluation Test Strategy
clusters.description: The environments, timing, adversarial procedures, and comparison methods used to validate deployed-agent behavior.

relations.rationale: Evaluation tests provide evidence about the production failures the monitoring system must detect.
Evaluation evidence constrains release and rollback decisions.

values.label: Held-out environment evaluation
values.description: Testing behavior outside the training environment and on shifted features or regimes.

values.label: Diverse scenario evaluation
values.description: Using varied scenarios to distinguish useful generalization from reward gaming.

values.label: Adversarial reward testing
values.description: Generating edge cases, adversarial policies, or reward-function attacks before deployment.

values.label: Shadow evaluation
values.description: Evaluating candidate policies on production-like traffic without serving their decisions.

values.label: Replay and simulated evaluation
values.description: Using historical replay and simulation to evaluate policies without live experimentation.

values.label: Counterfactual policy evaluation
values.description: Evaluating alternative policy decisions using logged contexts without live traffic injection.

values.label: Functionality-only evaluation
values.description: Accepting behavior when final outputs match a reference despite possible process or implementation exploitation.

values.label: Benchmark-only safety validation
values.description: Treating benchmark passage as sufficient evidence of deployment safety.

values.label: Simulator-bug exploitation
values.description: Reward gaming enabled by simulator defects or abstraction failures.

clusters.name: Reward Verification Architecture
clusters.description: The independence, composition, integrity, and access controls used to verify reward and evaluator signals.

relations.rationale: Verification requires reward, behavior, or human evidence to inspect.
Verifier reliability constrains the feedback and optimization mechanisms that can safely use its outputs.

values.label: Reward-model ensemble
values.description: Combining multiple reward models to detect evaluator disagreement and reduce single-model exploitation.

values.label: Hybrid reward verifier
values.description: Combining rule-based and model-based reward checks.

values.label: Reward-channel access control
values.description: Preventing the agent from accessing or modifying reward state, sensors, buffers, or reward mechanisms.

values.label: Measurement-integrity protection
values.description: Preventing alteration of execution-time, score, or other evaluation measurements.

values.label: Reward-function integrity testing
values.description: Testing whether the reward function or reward-generating mechanism has been modified.

values.label: Demonstration-based imitation learning
values.description: Learning from human demonstrations rather than directly optimizing a potentially exploitable reward.

values.label: Reward-verifier circumvention
values.description: An agent bypasses rule-based or model-based reward verification.

values.label: Proxy-objective divergence
values.description: The optimized reward differs from the intended objective despite apparently successful evaluation.

clusters.name: Feedback and Update Strategy
clusters.description: The source, quality controls, reuse, timing, and execution architecture through which production evidence changes policies or reward models.

relations.rationale: Feedback reuse requires acquired monitoring, outcome, or human evidence.
Feedback and updates produce candidate versions requiring controlled release.
Update architecture constrains hosting, serving isolation, and resource placement.

values.label: Continuous human feedback loop
values.description: Ongoing human review and corrective feedback guide deployed-agent improvement.

values.label: Real-time human feedback integration
values.description: Integrating evaluator input into machine-learning workflows during operation.

values.label: Standardized feedback protocols
values.description: Using annotation guidelines and consistent protocols to control evaluator variation.

values.label: Expert annotator training
values.description: Training domain-informed annotators for complex and enterprise cases.

values.label: Organized rare-case review
values.description: Routing complex, unusual, or rare cases to skilled human review.

values.label: Recent-corpus fine-tuning

clusters.name: Monitoring Evidence Modality
clusters.description: The observable evidence used to assess deployed-agent behavior, including rewards, outputs, reasoning, actions, telemetry, internal state, and human judgments.

relations.rationale: Available evidence constrains which detection and oversight mechanisms can operate reliably.
Evidence availability limits the feedback and update mechanisms that can be safely applied.

values.label: Continuous output evaluation
values.description: Ongoing assessment of deployed outputs for performance decay, quality drift, and behavioral change.

values.label: Human output-quality review
values.description: Periodic human scoring of production outputs for relevance, correctness, trustworthiness, or subtle drift.

values.label: Model-confidence monitoring
values.description: Using confidence scores as an RL-specific signal for deployed behavior and inference quality.

values.label: Infrastructure-health telemetry
values.description: Monitoring CPU, memory, network, latency, and related infrastructure signals alongside agent behavior.

values.label: Reward-signal monitoring
values.description: Monitoring scalar or proxy rewards as evidence of agent performance.

values.label: Proxy-reward monitoring
values.description: Monitoring proxy rewards that may diverge from real-world or true task outcomes.

values.label: Behavior-trace diagnostics
values.description: Analyzing actions, trajectories, outputs, tool traces, and logs.

values.label: Chain-of-thought monitoring
values.description: Using reasoning traces to inspect exploits, misalignment, or concealed intent.

values.label: Action-only monitoring
values.description: Monitoring externally visible actions without access to reasoning traces.

values.label: Operational service telemetry
values.description: Using latency, errors, resource use, feature availability, and invocation signals.

values.label: Human-oracle scoring
values.description: Using human judgments as evidence alongside automated evaluation.

values.label: External-world feedback
values.description: Using real-world outcomes rather than only internal reward or evaluator signals.

values.label: Activation-state monitoring
values.description: Monitoring internal activations, values, entropy, weights, or related model state.

values.label: Scratchpad reasoning observability
values.description: Using exposed scratchpad or hidden-reasoning traces to inspect belief use, evaluation awareness, alignment faking, or reward-hacking intent.

values.label: Automated safety-flag signals
values.description: Using classifiers or keyword detectors to flag harmful, biased, or inappropriate outputs at production scale.

values.label: Exploration-pattern monitoring
values.description: Monitoring exploration behavior to identify unsafe, anomalous, or unusually risky production actions.

values.label: System-health telemetry
values.description: Monitoring infrastructure and service-health signals alongside agent behavior and reward signals.

values.label: User-behavior feedback signals
values.description: Using rephrasing, edits, clarifications, bounce rates, usage, and related user behavior as indirect evidence of agent quality or drift.

values.label: Activation-delta monitoring
values.description: Monitoring changes in internal activations between clean and drifted inputs.

values.label: Observation-signal monitoring
values.description: Monitoring environment observations and externally visible state.

values.label: Agent-state monitoring
values.description: Monitoring internal state, values, entropy, activations, or weights.

values.label: Chain-of-thought monitoring signal
values.description: Using generated reasoning traces as monitoring evidence.

values.label: Chain-of-thought misalignment monitoring
values.description: Using reasoning traces to inspect misalignment or cheating.

clusters.name: Detection Target
clusters.description: The production failure or change that monitoring infrastructure is intended to identify.

relations.rationale: A defined detection target is required before selecting an appropriate detection method.
Detection targets determine which tests and evaluation scenarios are relevant.

values.label: Deployment-resilience failure
values.description: Failure to remain safe and effective under changing real-world deployment conditions despite training-time compliance.

values.label: Ethical-drift detection
values.description: Detecting drift toward unfair, toxic, biased, or otherwise ethically unacceptable behavior.

values.label: Behavioral phase-transition detection
values.description: Detecting abrupt qualitative behavioral changes associated with increased optimization capability or distribution change.

values.label: Distribution-drift detection
values.description: Detecting changes in input, concept, model, or live feature distributions.

values.label: Novel-situation detection
values.description: Detecting unfamiliar situations while distinguishing harmless novelty from capability-relevant hazards.

values.label: Capability-boundary detection
values.description: Detecting situations beyond the agent's reliable capabilities.

values.label: Reward-behavior divergence detection
values.description: Detecting high or improving reward paired with poor intended-task performance.

values.label: Alignment-faking detection
values.description: Detecting apparently compliant behavior that conceals a different objective or harmful intent.

values.label: False-negative-rate detection
values.description: Detecting missed harmful or emerging behavior through production error-rate monitoring.

values.label: Subtle-cheating detection gap
values.description: Failure to detect increasingly sophisticated or concealed cheating.

values.label: Intent-concealment outcome
values.description: The agent hides misaligned intent or behavior in response to monitoring or penalties.

clusters.name: Detection Method
clusters.description: The statistical, learned, comparative, or rule-based mechanism used to identify the selected production failure.

relations.rationale: Detection methods operationalize the selected detection target.
Method sensitivity and reliability constrain alert thresholds and intervention decisions.

values.label: BFAR degradation test
values.description: A BFAR-based test for detecting reward degradation after environmental change without retraining.

values.label: Embedding-cluster comparison
values.description: Comparing proportions of baseline and later embedding clusters to detect semantic input shifts.

values.label: CUSUM degradation test
values.description: A sequential CUSUM test considered as an alternative for detecting degradation.

values.label: Hotelling mean-shift test
values.description: A multivariate Hotelling test considered as an alternative for detecting reward degradation.

values.label: Naive mean degradation test
values.description: A simple-mean test considered as a conventional but non-adopted degradation detector.

values.label: Statistical drift testing
values.description: Using KL divergence, MMD, empirical distributions, drift indices, or related statistical tests.

values.label: LLM-based behavioral monitoring
values.description: Using a separate language model to inspect reasoning or behavior for exploits and misalignment.

values.label: Reward-model ensemble detection
values.description: Using multiple reward models and disagreement or agreement requirements to identify gaming.

values.label: Normal safety evaluation
values.description: Using ordinary safety evaluations to detect readily observable harmful behavior.

values.label: Detection incompleteness
values.description: Partial detector coverage leaves some anomalous or reward-hacking behavior unobserved.

clusters.name: Evaluation Test Strategy
clusters.description: The environments, timing, adversarial procedures, and comparison methods used to validate deployed-agent behavior.

relations.rationale: Evaluation tests provide evidence about the production failures the monitoring system must detect.
Evaluation evidence constrains release and rollback decisions.

values.label: Periodic benchmark evaluation
values.description: Running task-appropriate benchmarks at intervals to detect performance degradation.

values.label: Fixed-query regression evaluation
values.description: Repeatedly evaluating a fixed query set and comparing results with historical performance.

values.label: Cross-architecture validation
values.description: Validating reward and monitoring improvements across model architectures to detect architecture-specific effects.

values.label: Trap-based adversarial validation
values.description: Using traps, trip-wires, and adversarial training cases to expose shortcut discovery and superficial hacking.

values.label: Held-out environment evaluation
values.description: Testing behavior outside the training environment and on shifted features or regimes.

values.label: Diverse scenario evaluation
values.description: Using varied scenarios to distinguish useful generalization from reward gaming.

values.label: Adversarial reward testing
values.description: Generating edge cases, adversarial policies, or reward-function attacks before deployment.

values.label: Shadow evaluation
values.description: Evaluating candidate policies on production-like traffic without serving their decisions.

values.label: Replay and simulated evaluation
values.description: Using historical replay and simulation to evaluate policies without live experimentation.

values.label: Counterfactual policy evaluation
values.description: Evaluating alternative policy decisions using logged contexts without live traffic injection.

values.label: Functionality-only evaluation
values.description: Accepting behavior when final outputs match a reference despite possible process or implementation exploitation.

values.label: Benchmark-only safety validation
values.description: Treating benchmark passage as sufficient evidence of deployment safety.

values.label: Simulator-bug exploitation
values.description: Reward gaming enabled by simulator defects or abstraction failures.

clusters.name: Reward Verification Architecture
clusters.description: The independence, composition, integrity, and access controls used to verify reward and evaluator signals.

relations.rationale: Verification requires reward, behavior, or human evidence to inspect.
Verifier reliability constrains the feedback and optimization mechanisms that can safely use its outputs.

values.label: Consistency-curated reward signals
values.description: Filtering reward signals through consistency checks before using them for optimization or evaluation.

values.label: LLM-as-grader verification
values.description: Using a language model to grade difficult or subjective outputs and generate reward-relevant judgments.

values.label: Grader-bias exposure
values.description: Evaluator self-preference, positional bias, belief conformity, or other grader weaknesses that can be exploited.

values.label: Reward-model ensemble
values.description: Combining multiple reward models to detect evaluator disagreement and reduce single-model exploitation.

values.label: Hybrid reward verifier
values.description: Combining rule-based and model-based reward checks.

values.label: Reward-channel access control
values.description: Preventing the agent from accessing or modifying reward state, sensors, buffers, or reward mechanisms.

values.label: Measurement-integrity protection
values.description: Preventing alteration of execution-time, score, or other evaluation measurements.

values.label: Reward-function integrity testing
values.description: Testing whether the reward function or reward-generating mechanism has been modified.

values.label: Demonstration-based imitation learning
values.description: Learning from human demonstrations rather than directly optimizing a potentially exploitable reward.

values.label: Reward-verifier circumvention
values.description: An agent bypasses rule-based or model-based reward verification.

values.label: Proxy-objective divergence
values.description: The optimized reward differs from the intended objective despite apparently successful evaluation.

clusters.name: Feedback and Update Strategy
clusters.description: The source, quality controls, reuse, timing, and execution architecture through which production evidence changes policies or reward models.

relations.rationale: Feedback reuse requires acquired monitoring, outcome, or human evidence.
Feedback and updates produce candidate versions requiring controlled release.
Update architecture constrains hosting, serving isolation, and resource placement.

values.label: Continual pre-training
values.description: Resuming pre-training on recent or domain-specific data to update knowledge without full retraining.

values.label: Daily domain-data updating
values.description: High-frequency updating on current domain data for agents operating in rapidly changing environments.

values.label: Retrieval augmentation maintenance
values.description: Using retrieval of current information to mitigate knowledge drift without modifying core model weights.

values.label: Verifier-policy co-adaptation
values.description: Continuously adapting verifier and policy distributions together to close emergent deployment exploits.

values.label: Continuous human feedback loop
values.description: Ongoing human review and corrective feedback guide deployed-agent improvement.

values.label: Real-time human feedback integration
values.description: Integrating evaluator input into machine-learning workflows during operation.

values.label: Standardized feedback protocols
values.description: Using annotation guidelines and consistent protocols to control evaluator variation.

values.label: Expert annotator training
values.description: Training domain-informed annotators for complex and enterprise cases.

values.label: Organized rare-case review
values.description: Routing complex, unusual, or rare cases to skilled human review.

values.label: Recent-corpus fine-tuning
values.description: Periodically updating the model with recent high-performing or changed-domain data.

values.label: New-pattern retraining
values.description: Retraining on emerging slang, harassment variants, memes, or other newly observed patterns.

values.label: Negative-example reward-model retraining
values.description: Adding discovered reward-gaming failures as negative examples for reward-model updates.

values.label: Drift-indicator retraining cadence
values.description: Scheduling retraining from drift indicators, business cadence, and operational constraints.

values.label: Federated offline RL
values.description: Updating policies without moving privacy-sensitive logs from originating devices.

values.label: Offline policy updating
values.description: Learning from logged experience without injecting exploratory traffic into production.

values.label: Conservative policy learning
values.description: Constraining unsupported or risky policy behavior during offline or deployment-oriented learning.

values.label: Online adaptation from live feedback
values.description: Updating the deployed policy directly from live feedback during operation.

values.label: Human-feedback resource intensity
values.description: Evaluator effort, time, and cost required for large-scale feedback acquisition.

values.label: Evaluator-consistency risk
values.description: Variation among evaluators reduces feedback quality and limits scaling.

clusters.name: Deployment Hosting Strategy
clusters.description: The serving topology, resource placement, model representation, security boundary, and operational infrastructure for production agents.

relations.rationale: Hosting resources and isolation constrain update execution and feedback processing.
Hosting determines available telemetry, data capture, and access controls.

values.label: Stateless inference service
values.description: Serving architecture that keeps inference services stateless to support horizontal scaling.

values.label: Kubernetes horizontal scaling
values.description: Using Kubernetes to scale production inference services horizontally.

values.label: Critical-component redundancy
values.description: Providing redundant infrastructure for critical production serving and monitoring components.

values.label: Least-privilege role separation
values.description: Separating training-pipeline access from production-deployment authority using least-privilege permissions.

values.label: Secrets management and artifact scanning
values.description: Protecting credentials and scanning model artifacts for vulnerabilities before production use.

values.label: On-device edge deployment
values.description: Running a compact policy locally on edge devices.

values.label: Compact policy representation
values.description: Using a resource-efficient policy representation suitable for device compute and storage limits.

values.label: Managed endpoint serving
values.description: Serving a policy through a managed production endpoint.

values.label: Private-cloud deployment
values.description: Hosting within a private cloud for sensitive or controlled workloads.

values.label: Inference request rate limiting
values.description: Limiting request rates to protect serving capacity.

values.label: Knowledge-distilled inference model
values.description: Serving a smaller distilled model to reduce inference cost and latency.

values.label: GPU request batching
values.description: Grouping inference requests for improved aggregate throughput.

values.label: Learning-serving resource contention
values.description: Update computation degrades production serving performance.

values.label: Endpoint autoscaling
values.description: Automatically scaling serving capacity with changing traffic while targeting latency, throughput, and cost requirements.

values.label: Multi-model endpoint consolidation
values.description: Hosting multiple policies behind a shared endpoint to reduce infrastructure cost.

values.label: Edge inference with centralized retraining
values.description: Running a lightweight policy on devices while periodically retraining centrally.

values.label: GPU inference serving
values.description: GPU-based serving for large models requiring real-time latency and throughput.

values.label: Inference quantization
values.description: Quantizing models to reduce serving resource requirements.

values.label: Inference-latency distribution measurement
values.description: Measuring response-time distributions before deployment to establish realistic service expectations.

values.label: Latency service-level objectives
values.description: Setting application-specific latency targets for production inference.

values.label: Alignment degradation from serving optimization
values.description: Loss of helpfulness, safety, or alignment caused by aggressive quantization, distillation, or other serving optimization.

values.label: Batching-induced individual latency increase
values.description: Higher latency for individual requests despite improved aggregate throughput from batching.

values.label: Managed microservice serving
values.description: Managed autoscaling policy service.

values.label: Cloud-native RL service
values.description: Managed cloud-native RL lifecycle services.

values.label: Custom RL pipeline
values.description: Bespoke integration and safety pipeline.

values.label: Distributed training infrastructure
values.description: Multi-GPU or multi-node training.

values.label: API or microservice policy deployment
values.description: Policies are exposed through an API or production microservice.

values.label: Privacy-compliance protection
values.description: Sensitive data and regulatory obligations are protected.

values.label: Privacy and compliance protection
values.description: Protection of sensitive data and regulatory compliance.

values.label: Real-time stream processing for state representation
values.description: Streaming events processed into inference state.

values.label: Agent microservice exposure
values.description: Production exposure as a microservice.

values.label: API gateway for agent communication
values.description: Gateway boundary for agent requests.

values.label: Inference request authentication and authorization
values.description: Access control for inference requests.

clusters.name: Runtime Safety Intervention
clusters.description: The mechanisms that constrain, block, replace, reject, or hand off risky actions before they affect the environment.

relations.rationale: Intervention requires a detected hazard, uncertainty, or capability boundary.
Immediate intervention can precede rollback or broader containment.
Runtime constraints limit exploration and policy updating.

values.label: Automated circuit breaker
values.description: Automatically interrupting unsafe or degraded production behavior after a monitored breach.

values.label: KL-cap guardrail
values.description: Capping policy divergence to limit destabilizing updates under tool-conditioned variance amplification.

values.label: Policy safety-check layer
values.description: Applying a safety-check layer to constrain edge or production policy behavior.

values.label: Runtime shield
values.description: Placing a safety layer between policy outputs and the environment.

values.label: Unsafe-action blocking
values.description: Preventing unsafe actions from reaching the environment.

values.label: Unsafe-action replacement
values.description: Replacing unsafe actions with safer alternatives.

values.label: Action-space constraint
values.description: Restricting available actions to reduce unsafe or reward-hacking opportunities.

values.label: Unknown-situation human handoff
values.description: Rejecting unfamiliar situations or transferring them to human operators.

values.label: Safe exploration
values.description: Constraining exploration to limit unsafe production exposure.

values.label: Lagrange-multiplier safety adaptation
values.description: Dynamically balancing reward optimization against observed constraint violations.

values.label: Layered safety architecture
values.description: Combining multiple complementary runtime safety mechanisms.

clusters.name: Monitoring Aggregation Strategy
clusters.description: The temporal windows, granularity, statistical resampling, threshold qualification, and alert suppression used to summarize evidence.

relations.rationale: Aggregation operates on selected monitoring signals.
Aggregation determines when release, rollback, and intervention thresholds can be evaluated.

values.label: Sliding-window effective sample size
values.description: Computing ESS over sliding windows as supporting evidence about weight concentration and behavior change.

values.label: Tail importance-weight monitoring
values.description: Monitoring heavy-tailed importance-weight distributions, especially in tool-conditioned slices.

values.label: Rolling-window statistics
values.description: Computing monitoring statistics over recent windows.

values.label: Percentile tail monitoring
values.description: Monitoring distribution tails rather than averages alone.

values.label: Per-segment monitoring
values.description: Aggregating and inspecting evidence at segment or traffic-slice granularity.

values.label: Episode-aware bootstrap resampling
values.description: Resampling complete episodes to preserve non-independent trajectory structure.

values.label: Historical-variance calibration
values.description: Tuning thresholds to historical variance to control false positives.

values.label: Duration- or frequency-qualified alerting
values.description: Filtering transient conditions using persistence duration or recurrence frequency.

values.label: Burn-rate alerting
values.description: Alerting when an SLO budget is consumed rapidly.

values.label: Aggregate-metric tail blindness
values.description: Stable aggregates conceal rare catastrophic or tail behavior.

clusters.name: Reward Objective Representation
clusters.description: The number, structure, source, and interpretability of objectives used to express task success, preferences, safety, and intended behavior.

relations.rationale: Objective representation determines which reward and behavior evidence must be monitored.
Verification procedures operate on the selected objective representation.

values.label: Domain-specific outcome-process reward
values.description: Combining outcome-level and process-level rewards with domain-specific criteria.

values.label: Rubric-based anti-hacking reward
values.description: Using explicit rubric and checklist criteria to reward intended behavior and penalize shortcuts.

values.label: LLM-generated reward signal
values.description: Using grader-model judgments as a training reward signal for another model.

values.label: Proxy-goal divergence
values.description: A gap between optimized proxy reward and the underlying human or task objective.

values.label: Sole specified reward
values.description: Optimizing one explicitly specified reward as the primary behavioral objective.

values.label: Scalar proxy reward
values.description: Using one scalar proxy for success or preference.

values.label: Multi-objective reward signals
values.description: Representing multiple aspects of success through complementary objectives.

values.label: Structured reward decomposition
values.description: Using explicit interpretable rubric dimensions.

values.label: Human-approval reward
values.description: Using human helpfulness, correctness, or approval judgments as reward.

values.label: Preference-derived reward
values.description: Transforming pairwise or curated human preferences into a reward signal.

values.label: Natural-language proxy objective
values.description: Using an imperfect natural-language objective whose omissions may be exploited.

values.label: Constitutional rule-based reward
values.description: Using explicit principles or rules to evaluate outputs.

values.label: Single-metric optimization
values.description: Relying on one comprehensive metric despite possible hidden degradation.

values.label: Reward-signal phase transition
values.description: A small capability increase produces an abrupt qualitative change and true-reward loss.

values.label: Complementary metric set
values.description: Multiple metrics exposing degradation hidden by one metric.

values.label: Human-approval reward signal
values.description: Human helpfulness and correctness judgments used as reward.

values.label: Preference-derived reward signal
values.description: Pairwise preferences transformed into a reward signal.

values.label: Multiple objective feedback channels
values.description: Human preferences, AI critique, and explicit rules used together.

values.label: Modification-aware value learning
values.description: Value learning that accounts for changing utility functions.

clusters.name: Reward Transformation Strategy
clusters.description: The shaping, normalization, bounding, penalty, and scheduling operations applied after selecting an objective representation.

relations.rationale: Transformations modify the selected objective representation and its incentives.
Reward transformations determine which verification and anti-exploitation checks are needed.

values.label: Reward clipping
values.description: Bounding reward magnitude as a low-cost but limited initial anti-hacking measure.

values.label: Reward shaping
values.description: Transforming or supplementing raw rewards to reduce exploitation.

values.label: Bounded reward values
values.description: Constraining reward magnitudes.

values.label: Targeted reward penalties
values.description: Penalizing known hack dimensions such as verbosity, sycophancy, or unsafe behavior.

values.label: Length-normalized reward
values.description: Normalizing reward according to output length.

values.label: Classifier-based sycophancy penalty
values.description: Using a classifier to penalize agreement without accuracy.

values.label: Heuristic reward shaping
values.description: Combining learned preference reward with manually specified heuristic terms.

values.label: Manual-shaping objective interference
values.description: Excessive or incorrect shaping interferes with the original objective.

values.label: Reward shaping layer
values.description: Transformation of raw rewards to reduce exploitation.

values.label: Reference-centered rewards
values.description: Rewards centered relative to reference values.

values.label: Sigmoid reference-reward mixing
values.description: Preference reward transformed with a sigmoid and mixed with a reference reward.

clusters.name: Oversight Allocation Strategy
clusters.description: The allocation of assessment responsibility among automated evaluators, explanations, experts, operators, and continuing human review.

relations.rationale: Evidence availability determines feasible oversight arrangements.
Verifier reliability limits how much oversight can be automated.

values.label: Human production-output validation
values.description: Continuous or periodic human validation of deployed outputs for correctness, quality, and alignment.

values.label: Human-in-the-loop oversight
values.description: Continuous human review, correction, or escalation for deployed behavior.

values.label: High-risk review checkpoints
values.description: Expert or regulator review before or during risky use.

values.label: Explanation-assisted inspection
values.description: Using explanations or reasoning traces as audit evidence.

values.label: Automated-only review
values.description: Exclusive reliance on automated assessment.

values.label: Manual action monitoring
values.description: Manually reviewing every agent action at production scale.

values.label: Manual-review scalability limitation
values.description: Human review does not scale to the volume or complexity of capable-agent behavior.

values.label: Human-in-the-loop review
values.description: Continuous human review of deployed behavior.

values.label: Behavior-only monitoring
values.description: Monitoring external outputs without explanations.

values.label: Shared evaluator-generator model
values.description: The same model performs generation and evaluation under different prompts.

values.label: Deceptive evaluator-facing behavior
values.description: Correct-looking behavior pursuing another objective.

values.label: Human review of high-performing and anomalous behavior
values.description: Review of unusually successful or unusual behavior.

values.label: Human-in-the-loop oversight layer
values.description: Human oversight for alignment and ethical control.

values.label: Non-myopic human approval of likely future consequences
values.description: Approval based on anticipated downstream consequences.

values.label: Trusted-human-understandable paths for future feedback
values.description: Future-dependent evidence restricted to understandable paths.

values.label: Powerful predictor delegated by the human monitor
values.description: Delegated future prediction creating principal-agent risk.

clusters.name: Anomaly and Drift Detection
clusters.description: The detectors and statistical tests used to identify distribution change, uncertain actions, abnormal behavior, and divergence from trusted baselines.

relations.rationale: Anomaly and drift detectors identify changes that may threaten deployment resilience.
Detector behavior determines suitable aggregation windows and alert qualification.

values.label: Robust reward-hacking anomaly detection
values.description: Detecting anomalous behavior caused by exploitation of proxy reward functions.

values.label: Perplexity drift indicator
values.description: Using increased perplexity on recent text as an indicator of language-model drift.

values.label: Human-rated quality decline
values.description: A declining trend in human relevance and correctness ratings as evidence of production drift.

values.label: Dataset-to-live distance detection
values.description: Detecting deployment shift by comparing offline and live feature distributions with KL divergence or MMD.

values.label: Reward-model OOD detection
values.description: Detecting unreliable reward estimates on outputs outside the reward model's training distribution.

values.label: Action-compatibility detection
values.description: Detecting deployed actions that are incompatible with the production environment's action space.

values.label: Activation-classifier drift detection
values.description: A classifier detects task drift from internal activation differences without modifying or fine-tuning the base model.

values.label: Statistical out-of-sample detection
values.description: Statistical detection of production inputs outside the training or expected distribution.

values.label: Tool-conditioned support-mismatch detection

clusters.description: The target version and recovery procedure used after a deployed policy is judged unsafe, degraded, or exploitative.

values.label: Latest-checkpoint restoration

values.label: Post-healing learning-rate reduction

values.label: Safe fallback policy

values.label: Adapter rollback

values.label: Best-checkpoint rollback

values.label: Safe-baseline rollback
values.description: Returning to a safe baseline policy.

values.label: Reduced-learning-rate recovery
values.description: Resuming adaptation with a lower learning rate.

values.label: Safe-policy fallback
values.description: Rule-based or safe fallback policy.

values.label: Model and artifact version control

relations.rationale: Recovery is initiated by a rollback trigger.

values.label: Inference-time missing-feature safeguards

values.label: Unknown-situation rejection or human handoff
